content.overview: Indian environmental law is a layered system of constitutional provisions, umbrella and sector statutes, specialised tribunals and judicially developed principles. The Constitution contributes Article 21 doctrine, Article 48A and Article 51A(g). Principal statutes include the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water Act, 1974, the Air Act, 1981, the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. Courts have recognised the precautionary principle, polluter pays and public trust as part of Indian environmental law.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Constitutional, statutory or both? (2) Which medium — air, water, forest, wildlife? (3) Board consent, EIA or NGT? (4) Which principle — precaution, polluter pays, public trust?
content.study:
Always route by medium and forum. Do not treat every environmental grievance as only an Article 32 petition when a Schedule I statutory path before the NGT is available.

No new case invented. Doctrine topics retain Vellore, M.C. Mehta and Kamal Nath from migrated files.

sections.heading: Constitutional layer
sections.body: Art. 21 (healthy environment doctrine); Art. 48A (State duty); Art. 51A(g) (citizen duty); remedies under Arts. 32 and 226 where maintainable.

sections.heading: Umbrella statute
sections.body: EPA 1986 — Central powers, standards, hazardous substances, penalties.

sections.heading: Sector statutes
sections.body: Water Act and Air Act (Boards and consent); Forest (Conservation) Act; Wild Life (Protection) Act.

sections.heading: Judicial principles
sections.body: Precaution, polluter pays, public trust, sustainable development — applied alongside statute.

examples.title: Routing an industrial pollution problem
examples.body: Identify water or air medium → Board consent under Water/Air Act → EPA standards if applicable → NGT for civil environmental relief → constitutional writ only if maintainable.

hypotheticals.question: Should every environmental case start in the Supreme Court under Article 32?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Many disputes belong first to NGT or statutory authorities; writ maintainability depends on the facts and alternative remedies.

distinctions.title: Statutory environmental claim vs constitutional writ
distinctions.right: Art. 32 or 226 where a fundamental right and maintainability are made out.

misconceptions.trap: Environmental law is only judge-made principles.
misconceptions.correction: Statutes and notifications are primary; principles inform interpretation and orders within that frame.
